text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German bunds stumble towards the close, tracking T-bonds lower and prompting a swift bout of selling after crumbling through key trendline support at 101.60. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.11, down 0/51 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts closed near the day's lows, dicing with close support levels, earlier provisional M4 money supply rose S/A 10.4 percent year/year in April vs expected 11.3 pct. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-27/32, down 20/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - June bond future hit with other bonds late in session on back of selling by U.S. funds in several markets, contract bounced off strong support at 129.46/50 and retraced higher on GLOBEX. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.58, down 0.06 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets fell suddenly towards close as sales in Bund prompted profit-taking in Btps, with the market waiting for rest of sample Italian cities' preliminary May CPI after Tuesday's data showed inflation running at 1.5 percent from 1.7 pct in April. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.35, down 0.54 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. treasuries were off lows in late morning trade, seller of bonds said to pressure market earlier, with narrower March trade gap seen positive for economic growth. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-18/32, down 09/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.95 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended down by more than one full point due to massive selling on comments attributed to the Bank of Japan's deputy governor. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.65, down 1.05 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw a broad range of currencies and structures tapped during a brisk session, with no one deal standing out. Russia announced dates for investor roadshows ahead of the launch of its third bond issue on international markets. They will begin in Seoul on June 11 and end in New York a week later.
